questions_for_integrator: At what progress does the single line loss occur on the oval, s-bend and slalom? Is it the same point on each track, which would point to a fixed feature such as the start or one bend?
Does steering_oscillation stay below about 0.2 at y 0.06 m, so that the forward lead is not causing lag-driven overshoot?

Is there any controller change, such as a small increase in kd or base_speed reduction on the tightest bend, that you think would hold the s-bend progress without losing the oval gain? Please say what you would change and why.

intent: Commit the best measured geometry (iteration 9/10: five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.06 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.8 kg, body 0.12 by 0.16 m) as the final design. No geometry change is made this iteration, so the result can be read against the known 52.985 score. The aim is to hold the oval gain and to see where the single line loss occurs on each track, so the team can judge whether the design transfers to an unseen shape.
learning: Across iterations 0 to 10, the forward offset is the only geometry lever that improved the score, and it trades oval progress against s-bend progress. The single line loss per run has resisted every geometry change, so the remaining gains are most likely in the controller. Because this is the final geometry iteration, the team should report the per-track loss point and any controller suggestion so the final unseen-track result can be understood.
rationale: The race evidence points to the forward sensor offset as the one geometry lever that moved the score. Iteration 9 (five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.06 m) scored 52.985, the best measured result. Oval progress rose from 0.138 (y 0.05 m) to 0.151 and oval score from 56.25 to 62.77. S-bend progress fell from 0.148 to 0.140, and s-bend score fell from 61.01 to 57.74. Slalom was unchanged at progress 0.097 with 2.0 line-loss events. Iteration 10 reproduced 52.985 exactly, which confirms the result is stable across the reruns. Line loss stayed at about 1.0 per run on oval and s-bend, and steering oscillation stayed at 0.10 to 0.14, so the robot is not jittering. The loss is a single dropout at a fixed point, and no sensing, mass, wheel radius or wheel track change in iterations 1 to 8 removed it. Those levers all lowered progress or left it unchanged. The 8 mm footprint (iteration 8) and 16 mm footprints with wider spans (iterations 1 to 3) are rejected, so 12 mm is the footprint to keep. Wheel radius 0.035 and track 0.16 (iteration 6) raised oval progress but cost s-bend progress, so the baseline dynamics stay. The unseen final track is of a different shape and I have no race evidence for it, so I do not interpolate to an untested offset such as y 0.055 m, which might lose the measured oval gain. I keep the measured best design (y 0.06 m) for this iteration and the final race. Expected result: about 52.99, with oval progress near 0.151, s-bend near 0.140 and line loss at 1.0 per run on oval and s-bend.
